readout_other: psychophysical pairwise comparison and sensation discrimination accuracy; local blood perfusion volume by laser speckle imaging (moorLDI2-HIR)
direction_notes: Fingertip stimulation evoked tapping, vibrating, electrical and pressure sensations depending on PRF and intensity, with differing local blood perfusion responses. Peripheral stimulation, not transcranial.
safety_notes: Thermocouple maximum temperature increase of 0.72 degC; estimated maximum rise 0.95 degC; participants told to withdraw the finger on pain.

timing.protocol_description: Pulsed ultrasound at 3% duty cycle with PRF selected per sensation (tapping 4-7 Hz, vibrating 14-24 Hz, electrical 63-72 Hz, pressure 80-88 Hz), 1 s or 2 s per stimulus (2 s in experiments 2 and 3), followed by 5 s rest in experiment 2 and 1 min inter-trial interval in experiment 3.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: To examine the effect of different FF on tactile perception and the induced local hemodynamic responses, two focused ultrasonic transducers with FF of 250 kHz (HN81C-750- 250KC, Pantsd Inc., China) and 500 kHz (IBP0.512, NDT Inc., USA) were separately used.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: The pulse duty cycle was set to 3% to mitigate the ultrasonic heating effects, while the PRF was manually selected by adjusting the electrical signal input to the amplifier.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The duration of each stimulus was set to either 1s or 2s during experiments, towards providing effective stimulation yet short enough to enable repeated stimulation in compliance with the FDA guidelines.
